paper.title: Active Preference Optimization for Sample Efficient RLHF

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual preference (dueling) bandit under BTL model with linear rewards, active context selection
unmapped: Learner chooses the context x from a given set X as well as the pair of actions (a,a') each round
Sub-optimality gap is the max over contexts of the reward gap of the learned policy against the Condorcet winner
Preference y ~ Ber(sigma((phi(x,a)-phi(x,a'))^T theta*)) with logistic link
settings.definition_quote: R(T) = max_{x in X} max_{a in A} { r*(x,a) - r*(x,pi_T(x)) } ... (a) theta* lies in the set Theta = {theta in R^d | <1,theta> = 0, ||theta|| <= S}. (b) Features are bounded, i.e., ||phi(x,a)|| <= 1

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual preference bandit under BTL (lower bound, hypercube actions)
unmapped: Learner chooses context and action pair; sub-optimality is max over contexts
settings.definition_quote: Let X be a finite set of contexts, Theta = {-1/sqrt(T),1/sqrt(T)}^d, A = {-1/2, 1/2}^d.

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual preference bandit, uniform context sampling (lower bound)
unmapped: Contexts sampled uniformly at random from a finite set X by the learner (uniform learner)
settings.definition_quote: Say an algorithm Alg samples T contexts uniformly at random from a set X and for each context x_t, picks two actions a_t,a'_t from a set A. ... Alg then solves an MLE on this data to obtain theta-hat, and learns a greedy policy with respect to theta-hat.

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual preference bandit with general (non-parametric) preference function class
unmapped: Preference function f* in known class F of functions X x A x A -> [0,1] with f(x,a,a')+f(x,a',a)=1 (realizable)
Condorcet winner exists at each context
Learner chooses context and action pair; R(T) = max_x f*(x,a*(x),pi_T(x)) - 1/2

conditions: algorithm is a Uniform Learner (uniform context sampling, MLE, greedy policy)
sample budget T much smaller than the number of contexts |X|

source.label: theorem:lower-bound
source.quote: There exists a problem instance $(\cX, \cA, \theta^*)$ for which the policy learnt by a Uniform Learner \texttt{Alg} under the budget $T \ll \lvert \cX \rvert$ suffers $\Omega(1)$ sub-optimality gap with high probability.

results.notes: Restated as Theorem 10 in appendix. Probability at least 1-2T/N. Instance has theta norm 2 log(N-1). Comparator is per-context best action (max over contexts).

source.label: theorem:active-learning-lower-bound
source.quote: Let $\cX$ be a finite set of contexts, $\Theta = \{-\frac{1}{\sqrt{T}},\frac{1}{\sqrt{T}}\}^d $, $\cA = \{-\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{2}\}^d$. Then, for any algorithm, there exists a parameter $\theta^* \in \Theta$ such that sub-optimality gap of a policy learnt by the algorithm after collecting $T$ samples satisfies $\mathbb{E}_{\theta^*}[R(T)] \ge \Omega(d/\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: Proof gives explicit constant d exp(-1/2)/(4 sqrt(T)) (appendix Theorem 11; sketch says /2). Restated as Theorem 11.

symbols.kappa: max over contexts, action pairs and theta in Theta of 1/sigma_dot((phi(x,a)-phi(x,a'))^T theta)

source.label: theorem:logistic-case-regret-bound
source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0,1]$. Under Assumption~\ref{ass:bound}, setting $\lambda = \frac{1}{4S^2(2+2S)^2}$ and $\gamma = O(S\sqrt{d\log(ST/d) + \log(T/\delta)})$, the policy $\pi_T$ returned by \texttt{APO}, with probability at least $1 - \delta$, enjoys the suboptimality gap $R(T) \leq O( \gamma \sqrt{S \log(1+(T/\lambda \kappa d)){\kappa d}/{T}})$.

results.notes: Gamma substituted; matches appendix Theorem 17 which states C S^{3/2} sqrt(...) with universal constant C. Implies O_tilde(d sqrt(kappa/T)). Knowledge of kappa not needed.

symbols.N_F: (1/t, sup-norm) covering number of the preference function class F

conditions: Condorcet winner exists for every context (Assumption 2)

source.label: thm:gen
source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0,1)$, and $\cN(\cF)$ and $d_\cE(\cF)$ be the covering number and Eluder dimension of $\cF$ respectively. Then, with probability $ \geq 1-\delta$, the policy returned by \texttt{APO-Gen} enjoys sub-optimality gap $R(T) \leq \widetilde{O}(\sqrt{{\log(\cN(\cF)T/\delta) d_\cE(\cF)}/{T}})$

results.notes: Restated as Theorem 19. For BTL, yields O_tilde(kappa d / sqrt(T)). Sub-optimality measured in preference probability.
